tickerText: [TENNIS] Carlos Alcaraz capped Turin with a 6-2, 7-6(7) Nitto ATP Finals win over Alexander Zverev for his first season-ending crown, and Arribage/Olivetti rallied past Arevalo/Pavic for the doubles title • [SQUASH] PSA China Open closed in Shanghai as Mostafa Asal edged Mohamad Zakaria 13-11, 10-12, 11-9, 13-11 and S. Sivasangari took the women's title by walkover after Satomi Watanabe withdrew • [BADMINTON] LI-NING Hong Kong Open finished at Kai Tak with Wang Zhiyi beating Pornpawee Chochuwong 21-16, 21-11, Anders Antonsen awarded men's singles after Kunlavut Vitidsarn pulled out, and Man/Tee, Tan/Thinaah, and Feng/Huang taking the doubles trophies • [PICKLEBALL] Proton Daytona Beach Open ended with five straight-game finals: Hunter Johnson over Federico Staksrud, Judit Castillo over Kiora Kunimoto, Johns/Waters in mixed, Bright/Waters in women's doubles, and defending champs Ge/JW Johnson in men's doubles • [TABLE TENNIS] WTT Star Contender Muscat wrapped Saturday in Oman with Shunsuke Togami and Honoka Hashimoto winning singles and Japan adding mixed and women's doubles gold as WTT Feeder Düsseldorf II opens Monday in Germany

newsItems.title: Alcaraz Clinches Turin
newsItems.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz beat world No. 1 Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6(7) on Sunday to claim his first Nitto ATP Finals title, rallying from 3-6 down in the tie-break to become the youngest man to hold all four majors and the season finale.

newsItems.title: Shanghai Crowns Asal
newsItems.excerpt: Mostafa Asal outlasted Mohamad Zakaria in four games to win the PSA China Open in Shanghai, while S. Sivasangari was awarded the women's crown after Satomi Watanabe withdrew from the final.

newsItems.title: Kai Tak Podium Set
newsItems.excerpt: Wang Zhiyi defended her Hong Kong Open women's singles title with a straight-games win over Pornpawee Chochuwong, and Anders Antonsen took men's singles by walkover after Kunlavut Vitidsarn withdrew injured.

newsItems.title: Daytona Five Sweeps
newsItems.excerpt: Championship Sunday at the Carvana PPA Proton Daytona Beach Open saw Hunter Johnson, Judit Castillo, Ben Johns and Anna Leigh Waters, and defending men's doubles pair Augie Ge and JW Johnson win all five finals in straight games.
